info.title: The Music Scene — Label Intelligence Platform (Demo)
info.description: Generated 2026-09-28 from the pinned route table (tests/regression/routes.test.js: 68 registered routes) plus handler reads in src/routes/*.js. Auth is bearer JWT (login returns {token}, 24h). Four routes are public: GET /health, POST /v3/auth/login, POST /v3/auth/forgot-password, POST /v3/auth/reset-password. All other routes require the bearer token; some additionally require the admin role. Error bodies are JSON {error: string}; this API does NOT use RFC 9457 problem details. EXPLICITLY NOT SUPPORTED (despite claims in the legacy HTML docs): API keys, webhooks, /tracks, real-time Spotify data, MCP server, ISRC/UPC/ISWC identifiers, currency-aware royalties. Data-honesty policy (Phase 1B): every metric carries a provenance block {source, observedAt, basis: measured|estimated, note?}. The Spotify integration no longer fabricates monthlyListeners or stream counts; it reports followers and popularity verbatim. Known data-quality caveats: several integrations report not_implemented; the Stats history table is never written so projections run on synthetic history; the artist development projection is a labeled placeholder until grounded in real inputs. Financial-data posture (2026-09-28, FINANCIAL_DATA_POLICY.md): the platform is a lens on the label's own sales/statements, not a financial custodian; payment integrations are read-only and opt-in (Stripe Connect, TEST MODE ONLY - platform subscription billing and label direct sales are separate). Money is integer cents with ISO currency codes. AI financial analysis is strictly user-initiated and opt-in: scheduled monthly reports never invoke AI by default, and dedicated AI financial analysis requires an explicit per-request acknowledgment that it is not financial advice.

post.summary: Create Stripe Checkout Session (setup fee + subscription)
post.description: Admin only. Creates (or reuses) this label's Stripe customer and opens a Checkout Session in TEST MODE combining the ONE-TIME setup fee (STRIPE_SETUP_PRICE_ID) with the recurring MONTHLY subscription (STRIPE_SUBSCRIPTION_PRICE_ID). Returns the hosted checkout URL. Idempotent per label: an already-live subscription returns 200 with alreadyActive:true, and an still-open session is reused instead of opening a second one. 503 when Stripe is not configured.

post.description: PUBLIC — no bearer token. Authenticity comes from the Stripe-Signature header, verified against STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET over the RAW request body (the server stashes raw bytes before JSON parsing). Handles checkout.session.completed (-> active, setup fee paid), customer.subscription.updated (-> status follows Stripe), customer.subscription.deleted (-> canceled), invoice.payment_failed (-> past_due) and invoice.payment_succeeded (-> active again when previously past_due). Unknown event types are acknowledged with 200 and ignored. 400 on bad signature, 503 when Stripe is not configured.

get.summary: Profile-integrity check: Spotify albums vs delivered UPCs
get.description: Admin-only. Compares each artist’s Spotify albums against the delivered releases (UPCs) in the catalog and alerts on unknown albums. Optional ?artistId= scopes to one artist. Matching is barcode-to-barcode: album UPCs are hydrated via the batch album endpoint (GET /v1/albums?ids=), which exposes external_ids.upc (verified against Spotify’s API reference 2026-09-28). UPCs normalize digits-only with leading zeros stripped, so a 12-digit UPC and its 13-digit EAN form compare equal. Spotify albums with no exposed UPC are reported as unverifiable (not unknown, not matched). A Spotify fetch failure reports status error, never clean.

post.description: Body {artistId, revenueSources?, splits?}. Integer-cents royalty math: splits are integer basis points summing to 10000 (default 7000/3000 artist/label); the label leg is rounded half-up and the artist takes the remainder so the legs sum exactly to the total. Only USD streams are summed; non-USD streams are returned in flaggedStreams, never mixed in. Invalid amounts (bare non-number/non-object, negative, NaN, Infinity) are rejected with 400. (verified 2026-09-29).

post.description: Admin only. Multipart upload (field "file"). Columns: isrc_or_upc,amount_cents,currency,period,source. amount_cents is an INTEGER (cents) — decimals are rejected; currency is a 3-letter ISO code. Rows keyed by ISRC/UPC must match an existing recording/release; unmatched rows are reported, not dropped. Returns a per-row import report. No DDEX. Imports are idempotent: (catalog key, period, source) is unique, so re-importing the same file reports repeated rows as duplicate rejections instead of double-counting.
